title: Independent track-provenance and after-action audit tool for C-UAS and unit drone operations, with a friendly-flight declaration adapter (MAVLink/GCS to CoT flight-intent extension) and an offline-first UAS operator/airframe qualification and readiness ledger
problem: After a counter-UAS engagement or a unit drone mission nobody can independently reconstruct which sensor said what, when, and why a track was called friend or unknown; friendly drone intent still reaches the C-UAS picture by voice and hand-marking; and units fielding thousands of multi-vendor drones track operator qualification and airframe readiness in DTMS entries, spreadsheets and binders.

user.exact_role: (a) JIATF-401 and JICO/ADAM-cell oversight staff, CTC observer-controller-trainers and range control officers who review C-UAS engagements and airspace incidents after the fact; (b) battalion S3 air NCOs and company drone team leaders who must declare friendly flights; (c) battalion sUAS master trainers and S3 sections who maintain operator/airframe readiness records
user.echelon: company to brigade for (b) and (c); CTC, range and joint-task-force oversight for (a)
organization_examples: JPMRC / JMRC / NTC observer-controller airspace cells (the community that wrote CALL Handbook 25-14)
Yuma Proving Ground / Falcon Peak exercise control (NORTHCOM, JIATF-401)
3rd Combat Aviation Brigade airspace management cell (BARS marking workaround)

current_workflow: 1. Friendly drone launch announced by radio/chat; unit marks it by BARS (bearing, altitude, range, speed) or an ATAK point; ADAM/BAE cell deconflicts procedurally per CALL 25-14 altitude blocks and ROZs
2. C-UAS sensors publish tracks into FAAD C2 or Lattice; operator correlates with the announced friendly flights under time pressure and labels friend/unknown/hostile

3. After an engagement, near-miss or exercise serial, the O/C-T or oversight staff rebuild the timeline from vendor screen recordings, radio logs, TAK chat and memory; the C2 vendor's own replay (where it exists) is the only machine record

4. Lessons learned are written into AARs and, at joint level, into products such as the JIATF-401 2026 Quick Reference Guide; no cross-vendor, government-owned machine-readable provenance record is retained

5. Operator qualification (sUAS Master Trainer course completions, currency), airframe and battery status are recorded in DTMS course-completion entries, unit spreadsheets, vendor clouds (Skydio Cloud) and paper logs; readiness is reported by hand
current_solution: Lattice (JIATF-401 common tactical C-UAS C2, $87M task order Mar 2026) and FAAD C2 with their built-in track logs and vendor-specific replay; TAK/ATAK with the free government UAS Tool plugin (MAVLink-class drones appear as CoT with telemetry and FMV); Auterion Mission Control CoT-to-ATAK feeds; procedural airspace control (CALL 25-14) and BARS hand-marking; DTMS as the Army system of record for individual training records; commercial fleet/compliance tools (AirData, Aloft, DroneSense - public-safety oriented); government test organizations and FFRDC data-collection teams at C-UAS test events (RECALL - not re-verified this session).
failure: Three distinct failures: (a) there is no vendor-neutral, government-owned provenance record that survives the exercise or engagement - the only machine record lives inside the C2 vendor's stack, so oversight staff cannot independently grade fusion quality or explain a friend/unknown call; (b) friendly-flight intent (window, geometry, purpose) is not encoded in the CoT the C-UAS picture consumes, so blue-ID collapses to voice and pattern-matching; (c) operator currency and airframe readiness across Skydio/Auterion/Gauntlet fleets have no unit-owned offline ledger, so readiness is re-typed by hand. The narrow form deliberately excludes live fusion and live friend/foe identification.

evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Because each of the three pieces is either already given away or already owned. The MAVLink-to-CoT bridge ships free in the government TAK UAS Tool and in Auterion's CoT feed, so no startup can charge for it; a flight-intent extension to CoT is a schema decision that belongs to the TAK Product Center and JIATF-401, not to a vendor. Operator/airframe records have a mandated home (DTMS) plus vendor clouds and mature commercial compliance tools, so a unit ledger is a spreadsheet replacement nobody budgets for. The independent after-action audit is the one function with real oversight value, and it is precisely the one startups cannot reach: the machine records live inside Lattice/FAAD C2 (CUI, vendor formats), the government already staffs independent measurement through test organizations and FFRDC data-collection teams at events like Falcon Peak (RECALL - not re-verified this session), and the customer's revealed preference in Sept 2026 was to make the incumbent stack itself the measurement baseline. Absence of a startup here reflects absence of a buyer, not an overlooked seam.
technical_wedge: A single ATAK-CIV plugin plus a small offline-first edge service that (1) emits a 'friendly-flight declaration' CoT event (proposed schema extension: flight window, launch point, altitude block/ROZ geometry, purpose, operator ID) generated from a MAVLink GCS or hand entry and pre-checks it against unit-authored ACMs; (2) records every incoming track/CoT event with source, timestamp and label into a tamper-evident local log that syncs opportunistically; and (3) replays and diffs those logs after a serial to show which source reported which track, when, and what the friendly declaration said at that moment. The audit engine is sensor-agnostic and could later ingest exported Lattice/FAAD C2 logs if a sponsor grants them.

mvp.what: ATAK-CIV plugin + edge service on a laptop/Android: friendly-flight declaration from a PX4/ArduPilot GCS, a unit ledger (operators, currency, airframes, batteries) that works offline and syncs via TAK Server, and an after-action replay that reconstructs a scripted range serial from 2-3 commercial sensor feeds (low-cost radar or RF detector, EO camera tracker, Remote ID/ADS-B receiver) with per-source lineage.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for all three pieces on self-collected range data with 3-5 commercial drones and 50-200 synthetic tracks; roughly 8-12 weeks for adapter+ledger, 4-6 months to add the replay/audit engine. Cost roughly $40-90k including hardware.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That (a) a declared friendly flight can be matched to a detected track with measurable precision/recall when cooperative signals are removed, (b) the replay reconstructs a labelled timeline that an O/C-T would accept as evidence, (c) the ledger replaces spreadsheet/binder tracking without a network - and, critically, that a named government sponsor will supply real exercise logs, without which the demo proves only that the plumbing works.

data_requirement.what: Track/CoT event logs from C-UAS C2 (source, time, label, confidence), friendly-flight declarations and GCS telemetry, unit ACMs/ACOs, and operator/airframe/battery/qualification records; for a credible military demo, exported engagement logs from Lattice/FAAD C2 and exercise ground truth.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: MVP: yes - self-generated MAVLink telemetry, commercial c-UAS sensor outputs, Remote ID/ADS-B, synthetic ACMs built from FM 3-52/CALL 25-14, synthetic personnel records. Credible demo: only through a sponsor (JIATF-401, a CTC, ATEC/test organization) - engagement logs are CUI at minimum and vendor-format; real unit training records contain PII; export-controlled CUI is effectively US-person-only (E07-F30), so the Indonesian co-founder cannot be assumed to handle that half. Needs counsel.

entry_vehicle.primary: Free ATAK-CIV plugin (flight-intent declaration + ledger) piloted by invitation with one TiC battalion or CTC O/C-T cell, then an xTech prize or a JIATF-401 CSO white paper for the audit engine once a sponsor supplies exercise logs
sequence: 1. Build plugin + replay engine on ATAK-CIV and PX4/ArduPilot with commercial sensors (no government paperwork; 3-6 months; <$90k)
2. Unit or CTC invitation for an unfunded pilot; TAK.gov plugin submission/signing for government users
3. xTech (sensor-integration / mission C2 problem areas) or the xTech hackathon for visibility; JIATF-401 industry demo day
4. CRADA or OTA with a test organization / JIATF-401 granting exported exercise logs to a US-person enclave for the audit engine
5. Only then: CSO/OTA award or a subcontract to a test-support or FFRDC team - realistically a services relationship
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires >50% ownership and control by US citizens/permanent residents (E07-F3): not met today, possible after the German founder's green card only if the cap table is structured accordingly; AFWERX-style rules bar a non-US-person from being technical lead on controlled work (E07-F7). TAK-CIV plugins, xTech, OTAs and CSOs carry no citizenship test (E07-F22). The audit half touches export-controlled CUI (engagement logs, C2 interface formats), which is effectively US-person-only (E07-F30); the Indonesian founder would need a technology control plan and, for any 600-series/ITAR data, a licence (E07-F17/F18) - constraints to scope with counsel, not legal conclusions.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes for two of three pieces within a release cycle: Lattice/FAAD C2 can expose track lineage, replay and a blue-drone declaration ingest as features (they own the data and the JIATF-401 relationship); the TAK Product Center can add a flight-intent field to the UAS Tool. The only piece they are structurally unmotivated to build is an audit that grades their own fusion - but the government already sources that independence from its own test organizations and FFRDCs, not from vendors.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a standalone company thesis. The adapter and ledger are features with a $0 government baseline; the audit is a services/test-support role whose data the startup cannot access without a sponsor and whose institutional owner (government testers) already exists. A startup could win a small pilot on speed and unit goodwill, but nothing here compounds into a defensible product.

capital_required.assumptions: PoC: two founders, commercial drones/sensors, ATAK-CIV, 4-6 months. Credible demo requires a sponsor-provided exercise log set, a US-person engineering enclave, an operator/O-C-T advisor on retainer, TAK.gov plugin signing, CUI handling and export counsel, and at least one exercise slot (travel, hardware); 9-15 months. Production: ATO under a host system, CMMC self-assessment, sustainment, and integration labor per unit/CTC - largely services. All figures are analyst estimates (HYPOTHESIS, MEDIUM).

Any exercise data above CUI and any Link 16/UC2 work require clearance; neither founder is eligible for years

regulatory_burden.explanation: The adapter and ledger on ATAK-CIV with commercial drones are low-burden (EAR99-level per E07; PII handling if real personnel data is used). Burden rises sharply for the audit half: C-UAS engagement logs and Lattice/FAAD C2 interface formats are CUI and likely export-controlled; exercise captures may be classified; government plugin signing and an ATO under a host system are needed for fielded use; CMMC self-assessment applies once on contract. Not a legal judgment.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder can build and demo the adapter and ledger today. The audit engine's real data (export-controlled CUI) is effectively US-person-only (E07-F30); ITAR technical data has no deemed-export exception for domestic foreign-person employees (E07-F18); a technology control plan and counsel review are needed before the first sponsor data set. The German founder's expected permanent residency resolves US-person status for export purposes but not clearance eligibility. Any allied (Bundeswehr) deployment could constitute an ITAR 'defense service' even for EAR99 software (E07-F15). Needs counsel.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Civil C-UAS sites (airports, stadiums, prisons, DHS/FAA test sites) need incident forensics and public-safety drone programs need currency/compliance ledgers, and both are fully unclassified - but those markets are already served by SkySafe/D-Fend/Dedrone forensics and AirData/Aloft/DroneSense compliance tools consolidating under Versaterm, so the dual-use beachhead is crowded rather than open.

defensibility.explanation: No data moat (logs belong to the government or the C2 vendor), no algorithm moat (replay/diff and record-matching are commodity), no interface moat (TPC, Anduril, Northrop and drone OEMs own every interface). At best a unit-adopted workflow and an O/C-T relationship - both non-transferable and non-compounding.

why_now: Friendly-drone density exploded (12,080 Gauntlet drones by Sept 2026, drones-to-every-squad), CALL 25-14 and BARS hand-marking document the procedural workaround, the $87M Lattice task order under a $20B enterprise agreement and Falcon Peak 26.2's 'baseline standard' role create lock-in anxiety that an independent record would answer, the Army CTO's NGC2 memo and DoD IG's Advana audit put logging/audit gaps on record, and ATAK-CIV plus the free UAS Tool make the plumbing trivial to build. What has not changed is that nobody has funded any of it.
killer_risk: There is no PROBLEM -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE path for any of the three pieces: the adapter duplicates a free government plugin and a schema the TAK Product Center controls; the ledger duplicates DTMS and mature commercial compliance tools; and the audit function - the only part with oversight value - depends on export-controlled logs the founders cannot access and on an independence role the government already fills with its own test organizations and FFRDCs, so the best outcome is an unfunded pilot or a test-support services engagement, not a company.

allied_extension: Marginally more compelling for the ledger and adapter, not for the audit. Allied armies fielding mixed Skydio/Quantum/Auterion fleets (Germany, UK, Poland, Ukraine) and NATO's interest in sensor-agnostic drone C2 (E06-F34) create similar readiness-record and friendly-declaration needs, and the German founder gives Cyber Innovation Hub / Bundeswehr pilot access (E06-F20). But allied C-UAS pictures run on national or SitaWare/Helsing stacks whose logs are equally closed, Ukraine already fielded its own UA DroneID, and furnishing the software to a foreign military may be an ITAR 'defense service' even if EAR99 (E07-F15). Allied markets change the buyer, not the absence of a budget line.
